name: screen-from-figma
title: Screen from Figma
description: Paste a Figma frame link. Reads the design and builds a matching screen in this workspace's own stack.

stages.title: Read design
stages.instruction: The Figma frame URL is in inputs.figmaUrl. Use the Figma MCP tools (e.g. mcp__figma__get_figma_data and mcp__figma__download_figma_images) to read that node. Produce a precise, implementation-ready UI spec: the component/layout tree, spacing and sizing, colors and typography mapped to design tokens, interactive states, and a list of any exported assets with where they were saved. Do not write component code in this step.

stages.title: Implement
stages.instruction: First detect THIS workspace's frontend stack and conventions from its .claude rules (e.g. .claude/rules/frontend.md), CLAUDE.md, and existing components — framework, styling system, component-wrapper conventions, and file layout. Then implement the screen from the design spec as new component file(s) that match those conventions exactly (reuse existing wrapped components; do not introduce a different UI library). Write the files into the repository. Keep it token-efficient and accessible.

stages.title: Review
stages.instruction: Review the generated component(s) against the workspace rules and the design spec: convention compliance, correctness, accessibility, and fidelity to the Figma frame. List any high-confidence issues with concrete fixes.

name: content-ops

name: feature-delivery
title: Feature Delivery
description: Take a feature request from a clear requirement all the way to a reviewed pull request. Best for building a new capability into an existing codebase.

stages.title: Clarify the requirement
stages.description: Turn the raw request into a crisp, testable requirement. Surface hidden assumptions and edge cases before any code is written.
stages.instruction: Restate the request as a short problem statement, list explicit acceptance criteria, and call out open questions or assumptions that need a decision.

stages.title: Technical design
stages.description: Decide where the change lives and how it fits the existing architecture — the modules touched, data flow, and the smallest sensible approach.
stages.instruction: Using the code graph, identify the files and modules to change, describe the approach in a few bullet points, and note any migration or contract changes.

stages.title: Implementation
stages.description: Write the minimum code that satisfies the acceptance criteria, reusing existing patterns and helpers rather than inventing new ones.
stages.instruction: Implement the feature following the design. Prefer existing utilities. Keep the diff focused; do not refactor unrelated code.

stages.title: Write tests
stages.description: Cover the acceptance criteria and the tricky edge cases with automated tests so the behaviour is pinned down.
stages.instruction: Add unit and integration tests for the new behaviour, including the edge cases raised during clarification. Ensure they fail before the change and pass after.

stages.title: Self-review
stages.description: Read the diff as a reviewer would: correctness, naming, error handling at the boundaries, and anything that would draw a review comment.
stages.instruction: Review the diff for correctness and clarity. Fix obvious issues directly; list anything that needs a human decision.

stages.title: Open the pull request
stages.description: Summarise what changed and why, so a reviewer can approve quickly.
stages.instruction: Write a pull request description: what changed, why, how it was tested, and any follow-ups. Keep it concise.

name: bug-fix
title: Bug Fix
description: Diagnose a reported bug, fix the root cause, and add a regression test so it stays fixed. Best when you have a reproduction or a clear symptom.

stages.title: Reproduce the problem
stages.description: Confirm the bug and capture the exact steps, inputs and environment that trigger it. A fix you can't reproduce is a guess.
stages.instruction: Establish a reliable reproduction: the steps, inputs, and expected vs actual behaviour. If it can't be reproduced, say what information is missing.

stages.title: Find the root cause
stages.description: Trace from the symptom to the underlying cause using the code graph, rather than patching the surface.
stages.instruction: Walk the call path from the symptom to the origin. Explain the root cause in one or two sentences and point to the exact location.

stages.title: Apply the fix
stages.description: Make the smallest change that addresses the root cause without introducing new behaviour.
stages.instruction: Fix the root cause with a minimal, targeted change. Avoid unrelated refactors.

stages.title: Add a regression test
stages.description: Lock the fix in with a test that fails on the old code and passes on the new.
stages.instruction: Add a test that reproduces the original bug and now passes. Confirm it would have caught the regression.

stages.title: Verify and summarise
stages.description: Re-run the reproduction, confirm it's resolved, and write a short note of what was wrong and how it was fixed.
stages.instruction: Confirm the bug no longer reproduces and summarise the cause and the fix in a few lines.

name: screen-design
title: Screen Design
description: Turn a product brief into a designed screen: research, wireframe, visual design, a clickable prototype, and a developer handoff. Best for designing a new page or flow.

stages.title: Understand the brief
stages.description: Clarify who the screen is for, the primary job it must do, and the constraints (brand, platform, accessibility) before sketching anything.
stages.instruction: Summarise the target user, the primary task, success criteria, and constraints. List any open questions for the product owner.

stages.title: Research references
stages.description: Gather patterns and prior art for this kind of screen so the design starts from proven solutions, not a blank page.
stages.instruction: Collect relevant UI patterns and examples for this screen type. Note what works, what to avoid, and which patterns fit our constraints.

stages.title: Wireframe the layout
stages.description: Lay out the structure and hierarchy — what goes where and why — without visual styling. Decisions about content and flow happen here.
stages.instruction: Describe a low-fidelity wireframe: the sections, their hierarchy, key components, and the primary and secondary actions.

stages.title: Visual design
stages.description: Apply type, colour, spacing and components from the design system to make the wireframe real and on-brand.
stages.instruction: Turn the wireframe into a visual design spec: typography, colour, spacing, and the specific components to use. Keep it consistent with the design system.

stages.title: Interactive prototype
stages.description: Wire the key interactions so the flow can be clicked through and tested for real.
stages.instruction: Describe the interactive states and transitions for the primary flow so it can be prototyped and clicked through.

stages.title: Design review
stages.description: Get sign-off on the design against the brief and accessibility before it goes to engineering.
stages.instruction: Review the design against the brief and accessibility guidelines. Approve, or list the changes needed.

stages.title: Developer handoff
stages.description: Package the specs, assets and states so engineering can build it without guessing.
stages.instruction: Write a handoff note: components used, spacing and states, edge cases, and anything engineering needs to know.

name: ux-review
title: UX Review
description: Evaluate an existing flow for usability problems and produce prioritised recommendations. Best for improving a screen or flow that already exists.

stages.title: Map the flow
stages.description: Walk the flow step by step and document each screen, action and decision point so nothing is reviewed in isolation.
stages.instruction: Document the flow as a sequence of steps: each screen, the user's goal at that step, and the actions available.

stages.title: Heuristic evaluation
stages.description: Assess each step against established usability heuristics (clarity, feedback, error prevention, consistency).
stages.instruction: Evaluate each step against usability heuristics. For each issue, note the heuristic violated and where it occurs.

stages.title: Prioritise the issues
stages.description: Rank the findings by user impact and effort so the team fixes the things that matter first.
stages.instruction: Rank the issues by severity and estimated effort. Group them into quick wins and larger changes.

stages.title: Recommendations
stages.description: Turn findings into concrete, actionable recommendations the team can pick up.
stages.instruction: Write clear recommendations for the top issues: what to change and the expected improvement.

name: story-writing
title: Requirements to User Stories
description: Turn a raw requirement or stakeholder ask into well-formed, prioritised user stories with acceptance criteria. Best for a BA or PO preparing a backlog.

stages.title: Gather context
stages.description: Capture the goal, the users involved, and the business value before decomposing anything.
stages.instruction: Summarise the goal, the personas affected, and the business value. Note constraints and anything ambiguous.

stages.title: Analyse and slice
stages.description: Break the requirement into independent, valuable slices — each one a story a team could deliver on its own.
stages.instruction: Decompose the requirement into vertically sliced stories. Each slice should be independent, valuable, and small enough to deliver.

stages.title: Draft the user stories
stages.description: Write each story in the As-a / I-want / So-that form so intent and value are explicit.
stages.instruction: Write each story as: As a <role>, I want <capability>, so that <benefit>. Keep them concise and outcome-focused.

stages.title: Acceptance criteria
stages.description: Define done for each story with testable Given/When/Then criteria the team and QA can rely on.
stages.instruction: For each story, write Given/When/Then acceptance criteria that are specific and testable.

stages.title: Prioritise
stages.description: Order the stories by value and dependency so the backlog reads top to bottom.
stages.instruction: Order the stories by value and dependencies. Note which are must-have for the first release.

stages.title: Stakeholder review
stages.description: Confirm the stories reflect intent before they enter the backlog.
stages.instruction: Review the stories and acceptance criteria against the original ask. Approve, or list what to change.

name: prd-authoring
title: PRD Authoring
description: Draft a clear product requirements document from a problem statement: goals, scope, flows and requirements. Best for a PO framing a new initiative.

stages.title: Frame the problem
stages.description: State the problem, who has it, and why it matters now — the foundation the whole document rests on.
stages.instruction: Write a sharp problem statement: who is affected, the pain, and why solving it now matters.

stages.title: Goals and metrics
stages.description: Define what success looks like with measurable outcomes, not features.
stages.instruction: Define the goals and the metrics that will show success. Keep them measurable and outcome-oriented.

stages.title: Scope
stages.description: Draw a clear line around what's in and what's explicitly out for this release.
stages.instruction: List what is in scope and, just as important, what is out of scope for this release.

stages.title: User flows
stages.description: Describe the key journeys the product must support so requirements have context.
stages.instruction: Describe the primary user flows step by step, including the main alternative paths.

stages.title: Requirements
stages.description: Enumerate the functional and non-functional requirements the flows imply.
stages.instruction: List functional and non-functional requirements derived from the flows. Make each one testable.

stages.title: Review
stages.description: Check the document is complete and coherent before circulating it.
stages.instruction: Review the PRD for completeness and internal consistency. Approve, or list gaps to fill.

name: test-planning
title: Test Planning
description: Build a structured test plan from a requirement: scenarios, cases, data and a results report. Best for QA preparing coverage for a feature.

stages.title: Analyse requirements
stages.description: Read the requirement and acceptance criteria and pull out everything that must be verified, including the unhappy paths.
stages.instruction: Extract the behaviours to verify from the requirement and acceptance criteria. List happy paths, edge cases, and error paths.

stages.title: Identify test scenarios
stages.description: Group the behaviours into scenarios so coverage is organised and nothing is missed.
stages.instruction: Organise the behaviours into test scenarios grouped by area. Ensure each acceptance criterion is covered.

stages.title: Write test cases
stages.description: Write concrete, repeatable cases with steps and expected results for each scenario.
stages.instruction: For each scenario, write test cases: preconditions, steps, expected result. Keep them concrete and repeatable.

stages.title: Define test data
stages.description: Specify the inputs and fixtures each case needs so tests are reproducible.
stages.instruction: List the test data and fixtures each case requires, including boundary and invalid values.

stages.title: Execute
stages.description: Run the cases (or drive automation) and record pass/fail against each.
stages.instruction: Execute the test cases and record the outcome of each with any observations.

stages.title: Report results
stages.description: Summarise coverage, pass rate and any defects for the team.
stages.instruction: Write a results report: what was covered, pass/fail summary, and any defects found with severity.

name: bug-triage
title: Bug Triage
description: Take an incoming bug report, reproduce it, classify it, and write a clean, actionable report for engineering. Best for QA processing incoming defects.

stages.title: Reproduce
stages.description: Confirm the report and capture exact, minimal steps to reproduce. Unreproducible reports go back with questions.
stages.instruction: Reproduce the reported issue and capture the minimal steps, environment, and actual vs expected behaviour. If it can't be reproduced, list what's missing.

stages.title: Classify severity
stages.description: Assess impact and frequency to assign a severity and priority the team can trust.
stages.instruction: Assign a severity and priority based on user impact and frequency. Justify the rating in one line.

stages.title: Root-cause hint
stages.description: Point engineering in the right direction with the likely area or component involved.
stages.instruction: Suggest the likely area or component involved and any evidence, to shorten the developer's investigation.

stages.title: Write the bug report
stages.description: Produce a clean report: title, steps, expected vs actual, severity, and the root-cause hint.
stages.instruction: Write a clear bug report: concise title, steps to reproduce, expected vs actual, severity, environment, and the root-cause hint.
